questions.question: A company wants to rent virtual machines in AWS, keep full control of the operating system and installed software, store the instance data on virtual drives, and automatically scale the number of servers with demand. Which statement best describes how these capabilities map to EC2?
options: EC2 rents the virtual machines, EBS provides the virtual drives, and an ASG scales the number of instances
EC2 rents the virtual machines, an ASG provides the virtual drives, and EBS scales the number of instances
EC2 rents the virtual machines and EBS and ELB together provide automatic scaling of instance count
EC2 is a managed platform that runs the application and hides the underlying operating system
questions.explanation: EC2 is the IaaS offering: it rents VMs (EC2), stores data on virtual drives (EBS) and scales services with an auto-scaling group (ASG). Option B swaps the roles of ASG and EBS. Option C confuses ELB (load distribution) with scaling. Option D describes a managed platform (PaaS-like) model, not EC2 IaaS where you manage the OS yourself.
questions.keyTopic: Renting VMs, EBS, ELB, ASG roles

questions.question: A web application runs on several EC2 instances and must spread incoming traffic across all of them. Which EC2-related capability provides this?
options: An Auto Scaling Group (ASG)
Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)
Amazon EBS
EC2 Instance Store
questions.explanation: ELB is the capability that distributes load (traffic) across multiple machines. ASG changes the number of instances rather than balancing traffic; EBS provides network-attached virtual drives; Instance Store is hardware storage on the host.
questions.keyTopic: Renting VMs, EBS, ELB, ASG roles

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the sizing and configuration choices made when launching an EC2 instance?
options: Operating system choice (Linux, Windows or Mac OS)
Amount of RAM and compute power/cores
Route table entries for the VPC subnets
Firewall rules defined by a security group
questions.explanation: Route tables belong to VPC networking design, not to the EC2 launch-time configuration list, which covers OS, CPU, RAM, storage, network card, firewall rules (security group) and User Data. The other options are all explicitly listed EC2 sizing/configuration options.

questions.question: An architect needs storage for an EC2 instance and wants a drive that is reached over the network rather than physically attached to the host machine. Which choice fits?
options: EC2 Instance Store
Amazon EBS
A larger EC2 Instance Store volume
The instance's local host disk
questions.explanation: EBS (with EFS) is the network-attached storage option for EC2. Instance Store and local host disks are hardware storage physically attached to the instance's machine, so they do not meet the network-attached requirement.

questions.question: A solutions architect is comparing storage options for an EC2 fleet. Which statement correctly distinguishes the two storage categories?
options: EBS is hardware storage on the host, while Instance Store is reached over the network
EBS and EFS are network-attached, while EC2 Instance Store is hardware storage
Both EFS and EC2 Instance Store are physically attached to the instance's host
Only EBS is storage for EC2; EFS and Instance Store are not used with EC2
questions.explanation: Network-attached storage is EBS and EFS; hardware storage is the EC2 Instance Store attached to the instance's own machine. Option A reverses the categories, option C wrongly makes EFS hardware-attached, and option D ignores EFS and Instance Store as valid EC2 storage choices.

questions.question: An application team must allow only HTTPS traffic from the internet to its EC2 instances and block all other inbound traffic. Which EC2 configuration element is used, and when is it set?
options: A security group, set as part of the instance's configuration at launch
A security group, attached only after launch as a separate networking step
An instance store volume policy, set at launch
A User Data script that filters packets at first boot
questions.explanation: The security group is the set of firewall rules controlling traffic to and from the instance and is one of the launch-time configuration options. Option B reflects the misconception that firewall rules are a later separate step; Instance Store is storage, not a firewall; User Data is a bootstrap script, not a packet filter.
questions.keyTopic: Security group as firewall rule set

questions.question: A team launches a new Linux EC2 instance and needs a web server installed, package updates applied and a configuration file downloaded before anyone logs in. Which approach meets this requirement?
options: Supply an EC2 User Data script that runs at the instance's first start
Write a script that the team runs manually over SSH after every reboot
Configure a security group rule that installs the packages on first connection
Attach an EC2 Instance Store volume pre-loaded with the web server
questions.explanation: User Data bootstraps the instance by launching commands when the machine starts, automating tasks such as installing updates, installing software and downloading files. Options B and C do not automate boot configuration (security groups control traffic only), and Instance Store is raw hardware storage that does not install software.

questions.question: An instance bootstrapped with User Data is stopped and started again, and later rebooted. What happens to the User Data script?
options: It runs again on every start and every reboot
It runs again only after a reboot, not after a stop/start
It does not run again; it executes only once at the instance's first start
It runs again only if the instance's security group is changed
questions.explanation: The User Data script is run only once at the instance's first start, so restarts and reboots do not execute it again. The other options repeat the common misconception that it runs on every boot or is triggered by unrelated configuration changes.
questions.keyTopic: User Data runs once as root

questions.question: A User Data script must install system packages that require elevated privileges, and the team wants no additional permission configuration. Which statement about the script's execution identity is correct?
options: It runs as the root user, so it has full privileges on the instance
It runs as a limited default user and cannot install system packages
It runs as the IAM role attached to the instance rather than as an OS user
It runs as root only when the instance OS is Windows
questions.explanation: The EC2 User Data script runs with the root user, giving it full privileges for privileged boot tasks such as installing software and updates. Option B understates its privileges, option C confuses the IAM role with the OS user, and option D invents an OS-specific restriction that the source does not state.
questions.keyTopic: User Data runs once as root

questions.question: A startup wants AWS compute where it rents virtual machines rather than only running code as functions, and wants to choose the operating system, CPU and RAM per instance. Which description of the service is accurate?
options: EC2 is a serverless compute service where the OS is fully managed by AWS
EC2 is Amazon's Infrastructure as a Service offering, with sizing chosen at launch
EC2 only provides virtual machines and no related storage or scaling capabilities
EC2 is a database service that runs on top of EBS volumes
questions.explanation: EC2 is Elastic Compute Cloud, AWS's IaaS offering where you rent virtual machines and pick OS, CPU, RAM, storage, network card, firewall rules and User Data at launch. Option A describes serverless computing rather than IaaS VMs, option C forgets the EBS, ELB and ASG capabilities that are part of the EC2 offering, and option D mislabels a compute service as a database service.
questions.keyTopic: EC2 as Infrastructure as a Service
